parameter: a_coast (as originally formulated in Phase 0.2 - accelerator-release coast phase)
status: NOT_IDENTIFIABLE under the chosen Phase 1A baseline (retired, not merely unmeasured)
basis: control_ownership_timeline.md establishes that under baseline policy B (the chosen Phase 1A handover policy), automation holds v0 right up to t_reaction - there is no temporal window in which the vehicle is in an uncommanded/accelerator-released state before the human brake command. The parameter describes a phase that does not exist in this baseline.
what_would_upgrade_it: Would become identifiable again only if a later sensitivity test adopts baseline policy A (immediate withdrawal) or C (staged), reopening a genuine pre-brake uncommanded interval.
notes: This is a structural retirement, not a data-availability gap - no amount of additional raw-data access would make this parameter meaningful under baseline B, because the physical situation it describes does not occur under B.

parameter: regen-vs-friction response-speed differential (REPLACEMENT mechanism - see vehicle_response_model.md Phase 0.3 update)
basis: Reformulated mechanism: regen-blended brakes may have a shorter t_delay / faster initial t_buildup than friction-only brakes, because electric motor torque response is physically faster than hydraulic actuation - a well-established general engineering fact, but no source quantifying the SIZE of this differential (as opposed to its qualitative direction) was found in this project's searches.
what_would_upgrade_it: A source directly comparing t_delay or early-phase build-up rate between regen-blended and friction-only braking systems, ideally via instrumented vehicle testing analogous to Paquette & Porter (2014) but covering both architectures.
notes: This absorbs the causal role a_coast used to play (distinguishing regen-flavored from friction-only profiles) without requiring an accelerator-release phase that does not exist under baseline B.

status: LITERATURE_ONLY (friction-brake baseline value); DERIVABLE_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS method identified but not yet executed
basis: 0.05-0.17s from Paquette & Porter (2014), an independent instrumented-vehicle study - not derived from any raw file accessed in this project.
what_would_upgrade_it: A described, executable method exists: in D004's raw data.csv, pair the binary brake_padel_status onset timestamp with the continuous aEgo trace's first significant deceleration onset (assumption: binary flag onset approximates true pedal-press onset). This was NOT executed in this pass because no braking episode was located in the two windows sampled (see raw_dataset_forensics.md). Locating and extracting such an episode would upgrade this to DERIVABLE_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS with a project-specific number, or DIRECTLY_ESTIMABLE if enough episodes are found to report a distribution rather than a single value.
notes: Do not conflate the literature value (conventional hydraulic friction brakes, Paquette & Porter) with a regen-blended value - no source distinguishes these, per the reformulated parameter above.

status: DOWNGRADED in Phase 0.3 to COUNTERFACTUAL_ONLY (was PARTIAL in Phase 0.2 - adversarially re-checked and the prior anchor no longer holds)
basis: Task 7 re-audit: the 1.75-2.0s figure Phase 0.2 used could not be re-verified as measuring 'time to reach maximum deceleration.' An independent search found that pedestrian-collision-warning (PCW) systems conventionally trigger when TTC drops below 2 seconds - i.e. the '2s' figure is at serious risk of actually being a WARNING-TRIGGER THRESHOLD, not a build-up-time measurement, in the source Phase 0.2 cited (arXiv:2112.09074). The source PDF could not be re-parsed to confirm or rule out this reading with certainty either way.
what_would_upgrade_it: Full, careful re-reading of arXiv:2112.09074's actual methods/results section (not just a search-engine summary) to determine definitively what the 1.75-2.0s figure measures - or a different, independently verifiable source for vehicle build-up time specifically. The same D004 episode-extraction method proposed for t_delay would also yield t_buildup directly once an episode is located.
notes: This is the most consequential correction in Phase 0.3: a number that appeared 'PARTIALLY RESOLVED' in Phase 0.2's report should not have been used in a Gate A run without this level of scrutiny. Per the task's explicit instruction, it is NOT allowed into Phase 1A as a literature anchor until this ambiguity is resolved.

parameter: v_rolloff (numeric threshold speed and floor fraction)
status: COUNTERFACTUAL_ONLY (unchanged from Phase 0.2 - mechanism LITERATURE_ONLY, numeric shape remains unanchored after further searching)
basis: Multiple independent engineering sources confirm regen torque fades near standstill and that production EV control logic deliberately phases out regen in favour of creep torque at low speed - but no source anywhere in this project's searches gives a specific threshold speed (km/h) or fade curve shape.
what_would_upgrade_it: Either a manufacturer technical document, an instrumented low-speed EV braking test, or - most promisingly given this pass's findings - locating a genuine regen-deceleration episode in D004's raw aEgo/state_gas_pos/state_regen_break_enable traces near v->0 and fitting the observed fade shape directly. Not executed in this pass (no regen event captured).
notes: See Task 9 decision in PHASE0_3_REPORT.md: given this status, v_rolloff is retained only as an explicit COUNTERFACTUAL sensitivity axis, not as an input to the primary Gate A literature-anchored claim.

basis: ~8-9 m/s^2 from general (non-peer-reviewed for the exact figure) vehicle-dynamics engineering references; not derived from any raw file accessed in this project, since no hard-braking episode with near-peak deceleration was captured in the sampled D004 windows.
what_would_upgrade_it: A genuine hard-braking episode in D004 (or the 100Hz subset of D001, once access is obtained) would let a_max be read directly off the aEgo trace's peak magnitude - DIRECTLY_ESTIMABLE in principle, not executed in this pass.
notes: Held constant across profiles in the Phase 1A primary run regardless of its evidence class (per vehicle_response_model.md and experiment_A_spec.md), so its LITERATURE_ONLY status is less consequential for Gate A's core comparison than t_delay/t_buildup/v_rolloff, which vary BETWEEN profiles.
